what: The smoke quote names the tree of the checkout it runs in and the sha256 of the binary it runs, but nothing ties the two: a blaze binary does not carry the commit or tree it was built from (`blaze --version` routes to `Route::Version`, which prints the release version only), so a quote made in a fresh checkout of the head with an older binary would pass `verify`. The fixture sources of harness/v2/versus (hello, six) are also only Python strings in versus.py, so smoke.rs has to hold a second copy of the two programs.
cost: a hole in the proof the quote is meant to be, closed only by the loop.sh flow building and running in the same checkout; and two copies of each fixture program to keep alike
cause: no build identity is embedded in the binary; the versus fixtures keep their manifests on disk but their sources in versus.py
workaround: H-smoke-before-merge: build and run the smoke in one /root/loop.sh call in the checkout of the head
fix: embed the source tree hash in the engine at build time and have `blaze --version --json` print it; smoke.rs then refuses a binary whose tree is not the checkout's. Move hello/six's src/main.rs (with the body slot) into harness/v2/versus/<name>/ so versus.py and smoke.rs read one file
